title: Operators
summary: Calculate, compare and combine conditions, and know why === is safer than ==.

quiz.explain: `%` gives the remainder after division. 17 divided by 5 is 3 with 2 left over.
`===` compares value and type. A number is not the same as a string, so the result is `false`. (`5 == '5'` would be `true`, which is why `==` is risky.)

quiz.q: Which expression is true only when BOTH conditions hold?
quiz.explain: `&&` means AND: both sides must be true. `||` means OR: one side is enough. `!` flips true and false.

quiz.q: Complete the code so that it checks whether `n` is divisible by 2 with nothing left over.
quiz.explain: `n % 2` is the remainder after dividing by 2, and an even number leaves remainder `0`. Prefer `===`.
When one side of `+` is text, JavaScript joins the values instead of adding them, so you get the text `34`.

exercise.task:
In `operators.js`, write and export three functions:

- `isEven(n)` returns `true` when `n` is even.
- `canVote(age)` returns `true` when `age` is 18 or more.
- `isPassing(marks, attendance)` returns `true` only when `marks` is at least 40 **and** `attendance` is at least 75.

Each function must return a boolean (use `return`).
hints: Each function is one comparison, and the third one combines two comparisons.
Use `n % 2 === 0` for even, `age >= 18` for voting and `&&` to join two comparisons.
